reasons: Section 12.3 gives AbbVie (our party, the customer/optionee) an unqualified right to terminate 'for any or no reason' on 90 days' written notice, in whole or country-by-country, which lands squarely within the fallback notice window (60–90 days).

No early-termination fee or penalty is attached, and Harpoon's termination rights are confined to material breach (12.2) and insolvency (12.4) — no vendor convenience right — so the clause also beats the fallback on the vendor side.

Consistent with the playbook's classification semantics, a clause meeting the fallback on its material terms is compliant and is not redlined; the shortfalls flagged in the rationale (90 rather than 30 days' notice; no express pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts) are minor sub-elements correctly noted in the rationale rather than raised as a deviation.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a false negative from phrasing — the right is expressed as 'for any or no reason' rather than 'for convenience' — and does not undermine the substance.
No redline or comment was proposed, which is the expected output for a compliant finding; the cited text supports the compliance conclusion.
